messages:
sam (Spectra): morning — we're seeing sustained 429s on our Dedicated pool between 07:30-08:00 UTC. Customer reports TPS SLO breach (token/sec). any ideas?
elaine (support): sorry you're hitting this. can you paste the root request id or sample timestamped logs?
sam (Spectra): root id: `req_0a9f3c` — here are the error snippets from prod: ```
2024-08-04T07:34:12.123Z ERROR inference: admission_rejected reason=burst_credits_none pool_id=ded-12 client=spectra host=gpu-3
2024-08-04T07:34:12.124Z INFO admission: queued=12 active=28 headroom_tokens=0
```
andre (oncall-sre): seeing the same in infra logs. Throttle bot also flagged admission drops. @throttle-bot can you post the burst-credit ledger for ded-12?
throttle-bot: Burst credits remaining for pool ded-12: 0 (max=3000). Last earned: 2024-08-03T22:00:00Z. Credits were consumed by spikes at 07:10 and 07:32 UTC.
mike (eng-runtime): quick context — ded-12 has min_replicas=2, max_replicas=10, autoscale window=60s. When headroom_tokens hit 0, admission control will reject extra TPS and return 429. Looks like burst credit regen couldn't keep up with the traffic shape.
sam (Spectra): traffic was a short 8-minute batch ramp from a downstream job — spiky short bursts (10s bursts every 30s). we rely on burst credits for those.
elaine (support): did you see any noisy neighbor evidence? any single client saturating one worker?
andre (oncall-sre): checking metrics — one tenant (internal-test-suite) did 3x larger seq-len requests during the same window; per-host CPU on gpu-3 spiked and nvlink contention rose. possible noisy neighbor on that host.
mike (eng-runtime): that fits. The admission algorithm uses global headroom computed across replicas; if one replica is starved (noisy neighbor), headroom drops and credits are spent faster.
kia (cs): customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they want a fast rollback to avoid SLO penalties. options?
mike (eng-runtime): short term options: 1) manual credit grant to ded-12 (we can add N credits) 2) increase min_replicas to 4 (more base headroom) 3) move Spectra to a different pool (migration) 4) throttle/more conservative admission policy to favor fairness.
elaine (support): can we do 1 + 2 quickly? grant credits and bump min_replicas, then monitor. how long to enact?
andre (oncall-sre): I can grant 2000 credits and bump min_replicas to 4 on the pool. ETA ~5min. will monitor for node saturation.
throttle-bot: Admin action: credits_added pool=ded-12 amount=2000 by=andre at=2024-08-04T07:41:10Z
sam (Spectra): thanks. will that stop the 429s immediately?
mike (eng-runtime): it should reduce admission rejects by increasing spendable headroom. However if the noisy neighbor keeps hammering a host, individual replica capacity may still be reduced — autoscaler may remix pods but migration takes time.
andre (oncall-sre): bump applied: `kubectl patch autoscaler ded-12 --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/minReplicas","value":4}]'` — scaling traces: ```
2024-08-04T07:41:25Z HPA: desired=4 current=2
2024-08-04T07:43:50Z pods_created=2
```
elaine (support): monitoring request rate + 429s. sam, please let us know if you see errors after 07:46 UTC.
sam (Spectra): initial check: 429 rate dropped from 12% -> 1.2% at 07:47. good improvement. we'll keep an eye.
kia (cs): customer notified and asked for a post-mortem and assurance this won't recur.
mike (eng-runtime): medium-term plan: tune admission policy to weight by per-tenant recent history (reduce credit burnout by noisy tenants), and add per-host eviction detection for noisy neighbors. Also recommend headroom forecasting — track seq-length distribution and predict credit draw-down.
andre (oncall-sre): follow-ups: 1) run repro for noisy tenant on gpu-3 in staging (mike), 2) add alert for burst-credit delta > 1500 within 10m (elaine), 3) propose default min_replicas increase to 3 for pools with predictable morning batches (product).
elaine (support): will open support ticket S-4237 and attach logs + timeline.
sam (Spectra): thanks all. can you also include billing check? they worried credits usage will spike costs.
throttle-bot: Billing note: burst credits are free to the customer but consume provider headroom — dedicated overages billed under reserved contract thresholds. No direct charge to customer for credits.
kia (cs): will confirm contract details and follow up with the account.
mike (eng-runtime): final note — please paste any repro traffic patterns. if Spectra can share the small batch job schedule we can simulate and recommend autoscale windows or pre-warming.
sam (Spectra): will share job timestamps and sample request payloads (seq_len stats) in the support ticket. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
elaine (support): closing loop here; action items assigned and we've mitigated immediate impact. we'll keep this thread updated with the post-mortem.
